reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified. Sync path (beaconDataColumnsByRoot in request_manager.nim:176-194) validates only inclusion proof (L190) via verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof, bypassing the length equality check in verify_data_column_sidecar (peerdas_helpers.nim:362-364). Gossip path correctly calls verify_data_column_sidecar at gossip_validation.nim:596, but sync-retrieved columns skip this check. Block processor (block_processor.nim:687) calls verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs directly, which creates cellIndices array with length=column.len and passes (kzg_commitments.asSeq, cellIndices, column.asSeq, kzg_proofs.asSeq) to the nim-kzg4844 wrapper's verifyCellKzgProofBatch. If column.len != kzg_commitments.len or column.len != kzg_proofs.len, mismatched array lengths reach the C library. 01e requirement (file: outputs/01e_PARTIAL_W3B4_1771748827.json, lines 78-93) explicitly mandates: 'All input list lengths must be equal before batch verification proceeds.' Spec deviation confirmed. Attacker control: An attacker can trigger this via beaconDataColumnsByRoot P2P request by crafting DataColumnSidecar with mismatched column.len, kzg_commitments.len, kzg_proofs.len. Path type: attacker-triggered. However, exploitability depends on nim-kzg4844/c-kzg-4844 library behavior with mismatched lengths - modern crypto libraries typically validate input array lengths and return error rather than crash. Without verification of the specific library version's behavior (status-im/nim-kzg4844 wrapping ethereum/c-kzg-4844), cannot confirm this causes exploitable undefined behavior vs. graceful error. Classified as CONFIRMED_POTENTIAL pending library version analysis. Target: status-im/nimbus-eth2 (31% client share per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json deployment_context). Single-component impact caps at Medium severity (threshold: >5% network). Severity justified: if exploitable, single malicious DataColumnSidecar packet could crash affected nodes (31% of network), exceeding Medium threshold (>5%).
